title: The Lord My Shepherd Is
description: The Lord My Shepherd Is in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 23, part 3, headed “The same”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord my shep-herd is, I shall be well sup-ply'd; Since he is mine, and I am his, What can I want be-side?

lines: Since he is mine, and I am his,
He leads me to the place
And guides me in his own right way,
Tho' I should walk thro' death's dark shade
In spite of all my foes,
Nor from thy house will I remove,
Nor cease to speak thy praise.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
